config.title: Cross-functional collaboration

intro.title: Cross-functional collaboration
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple project planning simulation that models how engineering teams collaborate with product and design functions. You'll learn the core concept of defining clear interfaces and responsibilities between different functional roles to streamline workflows. The main constructs involved are role definitions, task handoffs, and communication protocols, using basic organizational diagrams and process flows. As a beginner, you'll practice setting up a collaborative framework that ensures alignment and efficiency across teams.
intro.usecase: Cross-functional collaboration is a core engineering leadership pattern essential for building complex, integrated products. In practice, this appears when developers work with product managers, designers, and data analysts to align on feature specifications for a new dashboard, or when coordinating API contracts between frontend and backend teams for a checkout flow. Concrete scenarios include co-designing user onboarding modals with UX, negotiating data requirements for admin panels with business teams, and establishing shared testing protocols for search filters across services. Mastering this ensures features ship with correct functionality and a unified user experience.

objectives: Construct a cross-functional collaboration framework by defining key roles and responsibilities
Implement communication protocols for different stakeholder groups within the project structure
Configure shared documentation systems that maintain consistency across functional teams
Integrate feedback mechanisms from multiple departments into the development workflow
Apply conflict resolution strategies when priorities between teams diverge
Initialize regular sync processes that align engineering timelines with business objectives
Render progress dashboards that visualize cross-team dependencies and blockers

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' library to enable component creation and state management for cross-functional collaboration.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from the 'react' package.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing core React features
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The React library and useState hook are imported and ready to use.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check the import statement syntax. You need to import React and useState from 'react'.

steps.title: Create the main CollaborationDashboard component
steps.instruction: Create a functional React component named CollaborationDashboard that will serve as the main container for the application. Return null from the component for now.
steps.hint: You can use either a function declaration or an arrow function. Make sure to export the component.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the CollaborationDashboard component here
steps.expectedOutcome: A CollaborationDashboard component is created and exported, ready to be the main container.
successCriteria: The CollaborationDashboard component is defined as a function that returns null.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the component is named exactly 'CollaborationDashboard' and returns null.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Check the name and that it returns null.

steps.title: Initialize state for team members
steps.instruction: Inside your CollaborationDashboard component, use the useState hook to initialize a state variable called 'teamMembers' with an array containing objects representing different functional roles (engineering, product, design, marketing).
steps.hint: Call useState with an initial array value. Each object in the array should have properties like 'role' and 'name' to represent team members from different functions.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a teamMembers state variable initialized with an array of objects representing cross-functional team members.
successCriteria: The useState hook is called with an initial array containing at least one object for each functional role (engineering, product, design, marketing).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your teamMembers state is initialized with an array of objects representing different functional roles (engineering, product, design, marketing).
steps.feedbackWrong: Inside the CollaborationDashboard component, use useState to create a 'teamMembers' state variable initialized with an array of objects for different functional roles.

steps.title: Create the main dashboard structure
steps.instruction: In your CollaborationDashboard component, return a container div with the CSS class 'dashboard-container' that will hold all dashboard elements.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a div element that has the specified class.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a div with the class 'dashboard-container' as the foundation for the collaboration dashboard layout.
successCriteria: The CollaborationDashboard component returns a div element with className='dashboard-container'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're returning a div element with exactly the class 'dashboard-container'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a div element with className='dashboard-container' to create the dashboard structure.

steps.title: Add collaboration initiation button and wire handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside your component that calls the startCollaboration handler when clicked. The button should have text like 'Start Collaboration' and be styled with basic CSS.
steps.hint: Add a <button> element with an onClick attribute that calls startCollaboration with the appropriate argument. You can add inline styling like style={{ margin: '8px', padding: '8px' }}.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: button with handler
<button onClick={() => handleAction('task')} style={{ margin: '8px' }}>
  Perform Action
</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button element appears in the dashboard that, when clicked, will initiate collaboration for a team member by calling the startCollaboration handler.
successCriteria: Button element is present with text content
Button has onClick handler calling startCollaboration
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your button has an onClick handler that calls the startCollaboration function with appropriate arguments, and includes some basic styling.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't properly configured. Remember to add a <button> element with onClick={...} that calls startCollaboration, and include some styling attributes.

steps.title: Add issue resolution button and wire handler
steps.instruction: Add a button inside your component's return statement that calls the resolveIssue handler when clicked, and conditionally display the current collaboration status.
steps.hint: Place the button after the team member list. Use the activeCollaboration state to show which member is currently collaborating.
steps.expectedOutcome: A functional button that resolves collaboration issues and displays the current collaboration status when active.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added both the resolution button and the conditional status display.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button or status display is missing. Review the instructions for adding the resolution control.
